case_title: Sanjay Puran Bagde & Anr. v. The State of Maharashtra
aggravating_circumstances: Premeditated intention, use of dangerous weapons, presence of all accused at the scene
high_court_outcome: Dismissed appeal of convicted accused, reversed acquittal of appellants
neutral_facts: The accused and the victim were relatives with a prior incident between them. On the night of the incident, the victim and his wife woke up, and while the wife prepared for cooking, the victim went to attend to nature's call. The wife heard the victim shouting and ran to the scene, where she saw two of the accused assaulting the victim with an axe while the other two held him. The victim was taken to the hospital and declared dead. The accused were charged with murder under Section 302 of the IPC read with Section 34. The trial court acquitted two accused, finding they did not participate in the assault. The High Court reversed the acquittal, finding a common intention among all accused to cause death.
